overview:
### Release pipeline: npm trusted publishing on tag push (Difficulty: 3/5)

This change turns the `v*` tag release workflow into a real distribution channel. Pushing a version tag now publishes `vori` to npm with OIDC trusted publishing and provenance, so no long-lived token is stored, and it still uploads the compiled binary to a GitHub release. The workflow pins every third-party action to a full commit SHA and grants `id-token: write` for OIDC. A new guard step stops the run when the tag does not match `package.json`'s version. The explicit `bun test` step is removed because `npm publish` runs `prepublishOnly`, which already does typecheck, tests, the doc-count check and `build:npm`. The README's "Known gaps" entry now says that releases exist.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["push tag v*"] --> B["checkout + setup-bun (SHA-pinned)"]
    B --> C["bun install --frozen-lockfile"]
    C --> D{"tag without v == package.json version?"}
    D -->|"no"| E["exit 1: tag/version mismatch"]
    D -->|"yes"| F["bun run build (compiled binary)"]
    F --> G["setup-node 24 + npm registry"]
    G --> H["npm publish --provenance (OIDC)"]
    H -->|"triggers"| I["prepublishOnly: typecheck, test, doc-counts, build:npm"]
    I -->|"fails"| J["publish aborted"]
    I -->|"passes"| K["package published to npm"]
    K --> L["action-gh-release uploads bin/vori"]
    class D,G,H,I,K chg
    class A,B,L chg
    classDef chg fill:#d6ffd9,stroke:#1a7f37,color:#111
```

**Riskiest area:** the release job's ordering and permissions. `id-token: write` and `contents: write` are in the same job, and npm publishes before the GitHub release is created. If the GitHub release step fails after a successful publish, npm has the version but GitHub has no matching release, and that npm version can't be republished.
